posts.body_html:
IF you want to talk about a variant of S. rubra ssp. rubra that's a pain to grow, well, here it is! This plant is very sensitive to having "wet feet" and I almost lost them all twice to rot! While I did lose some, those that survived were the stronger individuals, and I'm happy with what's still there.

Check out the one with the long lid on the left hand side-these definitely have a distinct look to them. That's the joy of growing out so many different populations from different locations:

posts.body_html:
Oh, tell me about it. Rubra ssp rubra is the plant I have had the most difficulty with in almost 20 years of Sarracenia cultivation.

You are dead right, at least in my experience, that they can be sensitive things that can fold at the drop of a hat. In my location, of all the Sarracenia species they are the most susceptible to the dreaded Fusarium wilt. Rubra ssp jonesii ranks next.

Maybe its our analogous climate thing again

Certainly those are some healthy looking specimens you've got there at the moment.

posts.body_html:
HI Kiwiearl,

The moment I tilted the tray so the rubras NEVER sat in water, they stopped rotting. The tayis on a slope so the other end is flooded with water, but it doesn't matter because the purp. purps. there don't care. It seems some populations are more of a pain than others...jonesii's were the worst here, but now they aren't ever allowed to sit in water for more than 2 days, and all the rot is gone as well. I've also observed that soils with mineral and salt buildup lead to rubras getting that fusarium wilt, so I leach them every so often to make sure they don't get that toxic buildup.
